name: MAX7219 4-in-1 32x8 LED dot matrix
description: Four red 8x8 LED matrices side by side (32x8 pixels), each driven by its own Maxim MAX7219 LED driver; the four chips are daisy-chained DOUT to DIN, so the whole strip is written over one write-only SPI-style serial bus (DIN, CLK, LOAD/CS), up to 10 MHz, with 16 brightness steps. Runs on 4.0-5.5 V and can draw about 1.3 A with every LED on at full brightness. Sold as: MAX7219 4-in-1 32x8 dot matrix module, FC-16 type (four 32 mm matrices on one 128x32 mm board, input header VCC, GND, DIN, CS, CLK on the right edge; output header VCC, GND, DOUT, CS, CLK on the left edge for chaining).
eli5: A long strip of 256 red lights in 8 rows that can show scrolling words, numbers or little pictures.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 4.0-5.5 V (use 5 V). Up to about 1.3 A with all LEDs on at full brightness, so feed it from a separate 5 V supply sharing GND with the board

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, shared with the microcontroller and the 5 V supply

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: Serial data in (MOSI) to the rightmost MAX7219, sampled on CLK rising edge, MSB first

pins.name: CS
pins.description: LOAD / chip select for all four chips: hold low while sending, rising edge latches each chip's last 16 bits

supplierQuery: MAX7219 4 in 1 dot matrix module FC-16 32x8
buildNotes: Wire the INPUT header (the edge with DIN, on the right when the text reads left to right). The other edge has DOUT and only feeds another module.

Power VCC from a separate 5 V supply of at least 1.5 A and join its GND to the board's GND: the datasheet gives 330 mA per MAX7219 with all segments on at 40 mA (RSET about 10 kOhm on FC-16 boards), so four chips can draw about 1.3 A. From a USB board's 5 V pin, keep brightness at 0-3 and avoid lighting most of the LEDs at once.
With VCC at 5 V the MAX7219's logic-high threshold (VIH) is 3.5 V. 3.3 V GPIO usually works with short leads, but a 74HCT125 or similar 5 V buffer on DIN, CS and CLK makes it certain.
Add 10 uF and 0.1 uF capacitors across VCC and GND at the module, as the datasheet recommends, to keep the multiplexing current spikes off the supply.
The chips power up in shutdown with a one-row scan limit and minimum brightness: the driver sets display test 0, scan limit 7, decode mode 0 and intensity, then leaves shutdown (register 0x0C = 1).
Every write sends one 16-bit frame per chip (4 frames) inside one CS-low burst; the first frame ends up in the leftmost block, because DIN enters the rightmost one.

driver.code:
# MAX7219 4-in-1 32x8 LED dot matrix (FC-16 module), MicroPython driver.
# From the Maxim/Analog Devices MAX7219 datasheet: 16-bit frames (D15..D8 address, D11..D8 used,
# D7..D0 data) shifted MSB first on CLK rising edge (SPI mode 0, <= 10 MHz) and latched on the
# rising edge of LOAD (the CS pin). The four chips are cascaded DOUT -> DIN: during one LOAD-low
# burst the first frame sent ends up in the LAST chip of the chain. On the FC-16 module DIN enters
# the rightmost 8x8 block, so the leftmost block's frame is sent first.
# Power-up state (datasheet): shutdown, scan limit 0 (one row), no decode, minimum intensity,
# display test off.
from machine import Pin
import framebuf

_NOOP = 0x00
_DIGIT0 = 0x01       # digit registers 0x01..0x08 = rows 0..7 (top to bottom on FC-16)
_DECODEMODE = 0x09
_INTENSITY = 0x0A
_SCANLIMIT = 0x0B
_SHUTDOWN = 0x0C
_DISPLAYTEST = 0x0F


class Matrix(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    """32x8 (8*num x 8) framebuffer. x = 0 is the left edge, y = 0 the top row.
    Use fill(), pixel(), text(), scroll() etc. from framebuf, then show()."""

    def __init__(self, spi, cs, num=4, brightness=1):
        # spi: machine.SPI(polarity=0, phase=0, baudrate <= 10_000_000); cs: GPIO number of CS/LOAD.
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.num = num
        self.buffer = bytearray(8 * num)
        # MONO_HLSB: byte (y * num + m) holds columns 8m..8m+7 of row y, bit 7 = leftmost pixel,
        # which is exactly one MAX7219 digit register on an FC-16 block (bit 7 = left column).
        super().__init__(self.buffer, 8 * num, 8, framebuf.MONO_HLSB)
        self._frame = bytearray(2 * num)
        self._all(_DISPLAYTEST, 0)   # normal operation
        self._all(_SCANLIMIT, 7)     # scan digits 0..7 = all 8 rows
        self._all(_DECODEMODE, 0)    # raw bits, no Code-B decode
        self.brightness(brightness)
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()
        self._all(_SHUTDOWN, 1)      # leave shutdown: display on

    def _send(self):
        self.cs(0)
        self.spi.write(self._frame)
        self.cs(1)                   # LOAD rising edge latches all chips at once

    def _all(self, reg, val):
        f = self._frame
        for m in range(self.num):
            f[2 * m] = reg
            f[2 * m + 1] = val
        self._send()

    def brightness(self, level):
        """0 (1/32 duty, dimmest) .. 15 (31/32 duty). Keep low on USB power: 4 chips at 15 with
        every LED on draw about 1.3 A."""
        self._all(_INTENSITY, max(0, min(15, level)))

    def power(self, on):
        """True = normal operation, False = shutdown (dark, display data kept)."""
        self._all(_SHUTDOWN, 1 if on else 0)

    def show(self):
        f = self._frame
        n = self.num
        for y in range(8):
            # Frame 0 travels furthest: it lands in the leftmost block (m = 0).
            for m in range(n):
                f[2 * m] = _DIGIT0 + y
                f[2 * m + 1] = self.buffer[y * n + m]
            self._send()

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from max7219 import Matrix

spi = SPI(1, baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CLK}), mosi=Pin({DIN}))
time.sleep(1)
d = Matrix(spi, {CS}, 4)
d.text('AB12', 0, 0, 1)
d.show()
print('text shown')
time.sleep(4)
d.power(False)
print('display off')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
